attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓Which parameters are used in the [call makeBee] block? How should these parameters be used in the function container?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓How can you set the [set velocity to] block and [if then] conditional to update based on the input in the [call makeBee] block? 

❓ In the [function makeBee] container, what are the Bee sprite’s velocity and “dizziness” parameters currently set to?


Solution: 

In the [function makeBee] container, (speed) bubbles should be placed into the vx and vy parameters in the [set sprite velocity] block. A <isBeeDizzy> block should replace <true> in the [if then] conditional.
steps.instructions:
Each time the project is run, the Bee sprite moves at the same speed and bobs in place. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Bee sprite’s speed is randomly selected and there is a 30% chance that it will be bobbing in place.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the [while] loop places the correct number of Bee sprites at the right time.

validationItems.text: Drag (speed) bubbles into vx and vy parameters in [set sprite velocity] block; Drag <isBeeDizzy> block into [if then] conditional.
validationItems.failureText: Check the values used in the [set sprite velocity] block and [if then] conditional.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓What should the parameters in the < > comparison block of the [while] loop be set to so that 6 Bee sprites appear?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ When should the [while] loop run until?

❓ How many Bee sprites should be on the screen for the [while] loop to stop running?


Solution: 

The parameter in the < > comparison block in the [while] loop should be updated so it reads: <(length of array (array of sprites of kind Bee)) < (6) >.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code! 


Fix the bugs in the code so that 6 Bee sprites appear on the screen when the project begins.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the [while] loop places the correct number of Bee sprites at the right time.

validationItems.text: Parameters in < > comparison block in [while] loop are updated to less than (<) 6.
validationItems.failureText: Check the parameters in the < > comparison block of the [while] loop.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints:
❓ Which container block repeats the code inside at set time intervals? 

❓ Which container should the [while] loop be placed in so that Bee sprites reappear every 5 seconds, while there are fewer than 6 on screen?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which container does the [while] loop run best in?

❓ Which container runs every 5 seconds throughout the project?


Solution: 

The [while] loop should be moved from the [on start] container into the [on game update every ms] loop.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the game is too easy! No new Bee sprites appear once  the Player sprite has collected the first 6.


Fix the bugs in the code so that every 5 seconds, Bee sprites reappear while there are fewer than 6 on the screen.

subgroups.title: Debugging While Loops

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the [while] loop places the correct number of Bee sprites at the right time.

validationItems.text: [while] loop is moved from [on start] to [on game update every ms] loop.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Green Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about [for index] and [while] loops. These loops can be used to control the placement of sprites on a tilemap and make something happen while a certain condition is true. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Around and Around
badges.description: Use advanced loops that offer more control options to repeat code in a project.

badges.title: Card Catalog
badges.description: Use a loop that counts from 0 to a given number to repeat a section of code.

badges.title: Waiting for Things to Change
badges.description: Use a loop that will repeat a section of code while a condition is true.
